plain_english_question: Does a structured repo-search workflow help the same coding agent find a useful change that a free-form 'improve this repo' prompt misses?

same_for_both.hidden_evaluation: same and unavailable to the worker

arms.label: Free-form
arms.description: Tell Hermes to improve the repo and let it choose where to look.

arms.label: Repo Scout
arms.description: Make Hermes understand the repo, list multiple opportunities, stress-check them, inspect ambiguous cases, rank them, then build the best small reversible change.

success: Repo Scout produces at least one independently accepted improvement while Free-form produces none.
invalid_run: Any broken starting checks, missing target, hidden-evaluation leak, or infrastructure failure makes the experiment invalid rather than a negative result.

amendment.reason: The previous run accidentally removed the file under test, so no search happened.
changes: Fail closed if the worker starting state is not green.
Replace several generic search prompts with one developer-friendly Repo Scout workflow.

stop_rule: Run once. Do not tune Repo Scout after seeing the result.
next_if_it_works: Repeat the same Repo Scout workflow on fresh hidden opportunities before attempting multi-step self-improvement.
